This would make stubbing with when(mock.oneArg(anyString())) also match a later call mock.oneArg((String) null), returning the stubbed value instead of null. Therefore this method plausibly explains the failures specifically involving anyString, especially MatchersTest::anyStringMatcher and the anyString assertion in AnyXMatchersAcceptNullsTest::shouldNotAcceptNullInAnyXMatchers.

This candidate does not explain the failures involving anyList, anyMap, anySet, anyCollection, or primitive-wrapper anyX matchers, but it matches the same defect pattern for the String-specific matcher.
